summary: Integer division by zero (SIGFPE) in divideInterval() when a rank has no local atoms (list->inum == 0).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:254-256: 'nAtomBlocks = calculateNumberOfIntervals(inum, atomBlockSize); if (nAtomBlocks > 100) nAtomBlocks = 100; divideInterval(atomBlocks, inum, nAtomBlocks);'.  calculateNumberOfIntervals (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:475-483) returns 'M = N/intervalSize' = 0 for N==0 and does not bump it because 'N % intervalSize != 0' is false.  divideInterval (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:461-472) then executes 'int intervalSize = N / M;' and 'int remainder = N % M;' with M==0.  The CPU base never reaches this code: PairPOD::compute() uses the blockMode==0 branch (src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:187-233) and the block code (pair_pod.cpp:236-239) is dead.
failure_scenario: Any MPI rank whose subdomain momentarily contains no local atoms (dilute system, strong load imbalance, or simply more ranks than atoms) -> list->inum == 0 -> integer division by zero -> SIGFPE / undefined behavior at the first force evaluation.
suggested_fix: Return early from compute() when inum == 0 (after ev_init and the per-atom array setup), or clamp nAtomBlocks to at least 1 in calculateNumberOfIntervals().

summary: In the non-shielded vdW branch the derivative term is multiplied by rij instead of divided by it, giving a vdW force wrong by a factor r^2 for force fields with vdw_type == 2.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1256-1260 (analytic kernel, 'else' == no shielding): 'exp2 = exp(0.5*alpha*(1.0-rij/r_vdw)); exp1 = exp2*exp2; etmp = epsilon*(exp1-2.0*exp2); evdwl = Tap*etmp; fvdwl = dTap*etmp-Tap*epsilon*(alpha/r_vdw)*(exp1-exp2)*rij;'.  The CPU reference src/REAXFF/reaxff_nonbonded.cpp:164-165 has 'CEvd = dTap * e_vdW - Tap * twbp->D * (twbp->alpha / twbp->r_vdW) * (exp1 - exp2) / r_ij;' and the table generator inside this same KOKKOS file, PairReaxFFKokkos::LR_vdW_Coulomb (pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:669-670), also divides: 'lr->CEvd = dTap * twbp->D * (exp1 - 2.0 * exp2) - Tap * twbp->D * (twbp->alpha / twbp->r_vdW) * (exp1 - exp2) / r_ij;'.  Note dTap here is already dTap/dr divided by r (pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1228-1233 adds d_tap[1]/rij), so the second term must carry the same 1/r.
failure_scenario: Any ReaxFF force field whose ffield header sets vdW type 2 (inner wall, no shielding) run with pair_style reaxff/kk and control->tabulate == 0: the vdW force term is scaled by r^2 instead of 1/r (a factor r^2 at r~3 A is ~10x too large and of the wrong r-dependence), so trajectories, forces and pressure differ from pair_style reaxff; energies stay correct, which makes it hard to notice.
suggested_fix: Change '*rij' to '/rij' at pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1260 to match reaxff_nonbonded.cpp:165.

summary: TagPairReaxZero unconditionally writes d_hb_num(n), but that view is only allocated when cut_hbsq > 0, so a run with hbond_cutoff 0 dereferences a null view.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1592-1599 'void PairReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::operator()(TagPairReaxZero, const int &n) const { d_total_bo(n) = 0; d_CdDelta(n) = 0; d_bo_num(n) = 0; d_hb_num(n) = 0; ... }' - no guard.  allocate_array() only creates it conditionally: ':1530-1533 if (cut_hbsq > 0.0) { MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_hb_num,"reaxff/kk:hb_num",nmax); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_hb_list,...); }'.  Every other use is guarded (:1629, :1764, :1851, :1900, :3327 behind 'if (cut_hbsq > 0.0)' at :1024).  cut_hbsq is set from the control file at :360 'cut_hbsq = api->control->hbond_cut * api->control->hbond_cut;' and the CPU style explicitly supports hbond_cut == 0 (src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.cpp:133, reaxff_forces.cpp:51, reaxff_init_md.cpp:56 all test 'if (control->hbond_cut > 0)').
failure_scenario: A control file containing 'hbond_cutoff 0.0' (the documented way to switch H-bonds off) with pair_style reaxff/kk -> d_hb_num is a default-constructed View whose data pointer is null -> segfault (host) or illegal memory access (GPU) in the very first TagPairReaxZero launch.
suggested_fix: Guard the write: 'if (cut_hbsq > 0.0) d_hb_num(n) = 0;' (or always allocate d_hb_num with size nmax).

summary: Only the two-body slice of the base-descriptor array bd is zeroed; the d3/d4/d33/d34/d44 slices are left stale when their Nij guards fail (the zeroing calls are commented out), whereas the CPU code zeroes all Ni*Mdesc entries.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:1415 'set_array_to_zero(d2, Ni*nl2);' is the only zeroing; :1436 '//set_array_to_zero(d3, Ni*nl3);' and :1445 '//set_array_to_zero(d4, Ni*nl4);' are commented out and there is no zeroing at all for d33/d34/d44.  The CPU counterpart starts with a full wipe: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:1797 'for (int i=0; i<Ni*Mdesc; i++) bd1[i] = 0.0;' and EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 does the same (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1207 'for (int i=0; i<Mdesc; i++) bd[i] = 0.0;').
failure_scenario: A block whose total pair count drops to Nij<=1 (e.g. a 2-atom dimer stretched beyond rcut after a step where it was bonded): d3/d4/d33/d34/d44 keep the values written on the previous step/block and are multiplied by the POD coefficients in blockatom_base_coefficients -> wrong energy and forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Restore an unconditional 'set_array_to_zero(bd, Ni*Mdesc)' at the top of blockatom_base_descriptors().

summary: 'neighflag' is read in compute() but never initialized on host execution, because init_style() returns early before assigning it.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.h:50 declares 'int neighflag;' and the constructor (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:47-67) never initializes it.  init_style() (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:89-96) does 'if (host_flag) { ...; PairPOD::init_style(); return; }' and only the non-host path reaches ':101 neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;'.  compute() then reads it at :192 'if (neighflag == FULL) no_virial_fdotr_compute = 1;'.  host_flag is 1 for every CPU-only KOKKOS build (:66 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK);' with LMPDeviceType == LMPHostType) and for the pod/kk/host variant.  Contrast pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:774 where neighflag is assigned before any early return that can skip it.
failure_scenario: Serial/OpenMP KOKKOS build running 'pair_style pod/kk': the uninitialized int happens to hold 1 (FULL == 1, kokkos_type.h:27) -> no_virial_fdotr_compute is silently switched on mid-run, changing which virial path Pair::ev_setup selects; otherwise plain undefined behaviour flagged by sanitizers.
suggested_fix: Initialize neighflag in the constructor (e.g. 'neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;' or HALF) and/or set it before the host_flag early return in init_style().

summary: thb_cutsq is hardcoded to 1e-5 instead of taken from api->control->thb_cutsq, so the control-file keyword 'thb_cutoff_sq' is silently ignored by reaxff/kk.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:365-366 'thb_cut = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(api->control->thb_cut); thb_cutsq = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.000010); //thb_cut*thb_cut;'.  src/REAXFF/reaxff_control.cpp:101-102 reads it from the control file ('} else if (keyword == "thb_cutoff_sq") { control->thb_cutsq = values.next_double();') and the CPU kernel uses it: src/REAXFF/reaxff_valence_angles.cpp:222 '(bo_ij->BO * bo_jk->BO > control->thb_cutsq)'.  The KOKKOS angular screening uses the hardcoded value at pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2574 'if (bo_ij <= thb_cut || bo_ik <= thb_cut || bo_ij * bo_ik <= thb_cutsq) continue;'.
failure_scenario: A control file with a non-default 'thb_cutoff_sq' (e.g. 0.001 to speed up the valence-angle loop): pair_style reaxff uses it, pair_style reaxff/kk keeps 1e-5, so the two include different sets of valence angles and give different energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Set thb_cutsq = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(api->control->thb_cutsq); in setup().

summary: TagPairReaxFindBondSpecies writes d_tmpid/d_tmpbo before checking the MAXSPECBOND bound and keeps writing past the end of the row for every further bond, since the error is only reported after the whole kernel finishes.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4400-4407 'if (bo_tmp >= 0.10) { d_tmpid(i,nj) = j; d_tmpbo(i,nj) = bo_tmp; nj++; if (nj > MAXSPECBOND) k_error_flag.view<DeviceType>()() = 1; }' - the views are created with second extent MAXSPECBOND (:4350-4351 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_tmpid,tmpid,nmax,MAXSPECBOND,...)'), so index nj == MAXSPECBOND is already out of range and the guard fires only afterwards.  The error is not acted on until FindBondSpecies() returns (:4374-4375).  The CPU base has the same off-by-one (src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.cpp:786-791) but calls error->all() immediately, so at most one element is overwritten there.
failure_scenario: With 'fix reaxff/species' on a structure where some atom has 25 or more bonds with BO >= 0.10 (MAXSPECBOND is 24, reaxff_defs.h:54): the kernel writes d_tmpid(i,24), d_tmpid(i,25), ... , silently corrupting the next atoms' rows (and running past the allocation for the last atom) before the run is finally aborted with 'Increase MAXSPECBOND'.
suggested_fix: Test the bound before writing: 'if (nj >= MAXSPECBOND) { k_error_flag...() = 1; break; } d_tmpid(i,nj) = j; ...'.

summary: The three-/four-body descriptor guards use the per-BLOCK pair count Nij instead of the per-ATOM neighbor count used by the reference EAPOD implementation, so atoms with 0/1/2 neighbours get non-zero 3-/4-body descriptors in pod/kk but zero in pair_style pod.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:1421 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nij>1))', :1443 'if ((nl4 > 0) && (Nij>2))', :1452/:1460/:1468 'Nij>3/4/5' - here Nij is the TOTAL number of (i,j) pairs of the whole atom block (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:274 'nij = NeighborCount(numij, rcutsq, gi1, ni);' over up to atomBlockSize=2048 atoms).  The reference used by pair_style pod is EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1248-1284) where the identical guards 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nj>1))', 'if ((nl4 > 0) && (Nj>2))', 'Nj>3/4/5' use Nj = number of neighbours of the SINGLE atom i (called from src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:216 with the per-atom nij).
failure_scenario: An atom with exactly one neighbour inside rcut (gas-phase molecule, evaporated atom, dimer scan): pair_style pod leaves its d3 block zero, pod/kk computes d3 = sum pc3*sumU*sumU != 0 -> different energy and force for that atom.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the guards per atom (numij(i+1)-numij(i)) inside the kernels, or at minimum document/verify that the block-level guard reproduces EAPOD; the safest is to zero the descriptor of atoms with fewer neighbours than the guard requires.

summary: PairReaxFFKokkos::Init_Lookup_Tables() builds the spline tables for every LAMMPS type pair without checking map[i] == -1, so an unmapped (NULL) type indexes reax_param.tbp[-1]; Deallocate_Lookup_Tables() conversely skips those pairs and leaks their arrays.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:509-531 'for (i = 1; i <= num_atom_types; ++i) { for (j = i; j <= num_atom_types; ++j) { ... LR_vdW_Coulomb(i, j, r * dr, &(LR[i][j].y[r])); ...' - no 'if (map[i] == -1) continue;', while LR_vdW_Coulomb dereferences ':626 twbp = &(api->system->reax_param.tbp[map[i]][map[j]]);'.  Both the init_md() copy loop (:426-429 'if (map[i] == -1) continue;') and Deallocate_Lookup_Tables (:591 'if ((map[i] == -1) || (map[j] == -1)) continue;') do guard on map.  The CPU reference src/REAXFF/reaxff_lookup.cpp:195-198 restricts the loops to types actually present ('if (aggregated[i])') and sets LR[i][j].n = 0 otherwise (:255).
failure_scenario: 'pair_coeff * * ffield.reax NULL C H' (a NULL type, common with hybrid or with fixed/wall particles) plus 'tabulate' enabled in the control file -> tbp[-1][...] is read out of bounds inside LR_vdW_Coulomb -> garbage table values or a segfault; even without a crash the six spline arrays of every unmapped pair are never freed.
suggested_fix: Skip unmapped types in Init_Lookup_Tables (set LR[i][j].n = 0 for them) and drop the map[] guard from Deallocate_Lookup_Tables so that whatever was allocated is freed.

summary: PairPOD::~PairPOD() lacks the mandatory 'if (copymode) return;' guard required of every base class a KOKKOS style inherits from.
evidence: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:107-159 starts directly with 'memory->destroy(rij);' - no copymode check - while PairPODKokkos sets copymode = 1 during compute (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:208) and its own destructor does have the guard (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:76).  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 1 requires the guard in the base-class destructor.
failure_scenario: Any future functor that captures the pair object by value (the standard KOKKOS pattern) would run ~PairPOD on the copy and free the original's memory -> double free / GPU crash.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (copymode) return;' as the first line of PairPOD::~PairPOD().

summary: Error message in pod/kk names the wrong pair style ('pair pace/kk'), copied from pair_pace_kokkos.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:107-108: 'if (neighflag == FULL) error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair pace/kk");' - identical text to pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:780-781 which legitimately refers to pace.
failure_scenario: A user running pod/kk with 'package kokkos neigh full' is told to fix a pace setting.
suggested_fix: Change the message to name pod/kk.

summary: Unconditional Kokkos::fence() plus std::chrono timestamps around every kernel, even though the timing output is never used (timing flag is always 0).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:63 'timing = 0;' and nothing ever sets it; comptime[] is accumulated at :277, :284, :291, :306, :1403, :1412, :1419, :1426, :1433, :1440, :1449, :1457, :1465, :1473, :1618, :1630, :1653, :1660 but never printed.  Each accumulation is preceded by an unconditional 'Kokkos::fence()' (:275, :282, :289, :304, :1401, :1410, :1417, :1424, :1431, :1438, :1447, :1455, :1463, :1471, :1617, :1628, :1651, :1658), which serialises the device queue ~18 times per atom block.
failure_scenario: Every timestep pays a full device fence per kernel; on a GPU this removes all kernel overlap and adds host-device round trips for no benefit.
suggested_fix: Guard the fences and chrono calls with 'if (timing)' (or delete the instrumentation).

summary: The host_flag branch allocates three fresh Kokkos views (d_numneigh, d_ilist, d_neighbors) on every single timestep instead of reusing them.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:221-229: 'd_numneigh = typename AT::t_int_1d("pair_pod:numneigh",inum); ... d_ilist = typename AT::t_int_1d("pair_pod:ilist",inum); ... MemoryKokkos::realloc_kokkos(d_neighbors,"neighlist:neighbors",inum,maxn);' inside compute().  Because host_flag is 1 for every CPU-only KOKKOS build, this is the default path there.
failure_scenario: Large CPU KOKKOS runs pay an inum*maxneigh allocation, zero-fill and copy of the whole neighbor list every step.
suggested_fix: Only (re)allocate when inum or maxn grows, as the rest of the style does with grow_atoms()/grow_pairs().

summary: Device kernels call the unqualified C library math functions instead of the Kokkos:: overloads required by the KOKKOS coding rules.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:632 'double dij = sqrt(...)', :643 'double y5 = sqrt(y4);', :644 'double y6 = exp(-1.0/y5);', :648/:651 'exp(-1.0)', :659-:672 'exp(-alpha...)', :678 'sqrt(2.0/(l_rmax))', :681/:689/:697 'sin(a*x0)', :684/:692/:700 'cos(...)', :754 'double dij = sqrt(xx + yy + zz);' - all inside KOKKOS_LAMBDA bodies.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::exp / Kokkos::sin / Kokkos::cos in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Portability: back ends that do not pull the C math functions into device scope (and future Kokkos versions) fail to compile or silently fall back to double precision.
suggested_fix: Prefix the calls with Kokkos::.

summary: k_scale/d_scale are allocated but never filled or read, and 'using MathSpecial::powint' is unused; k_cutsq is modified on the host but never synced (it is also never read on device).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:145-146 allocate k_scale/d_scale; grep shows no other use of d_scale in the file.  :120-121 set and modify_host() k_cutsq but there is no matching 'k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>()' and d_cutsq is never referenced in a kernel.  :40 'using MathSpecial::powint;' with no call site.
failure_scenario: No functional impact today, but the unsynced k_cutsq is a trap for anyone who later adds a device read of d_cutsq.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused scale views and powint using-declaration; if d_cutsq is kept, add the sync after modify_host().

summary: PairSNAPKokkosHost declares its virtual overrides without the 'override' specifier, unlike the sibling PairSNAPKokkosDevice.
evidence: pair_snap_kokkos.h:559-563 (Device) 'void coeff(int, char**) override; void init_style() override; double init_one(int, int) override; void compute(int, int) override; double memory_usage() override;' versus :578-582 (Host) 'void coeff(int, char**); void init_style(); double init_one(int, int); void compute(int, int); double memory_usage();'.
failure_scenario: If a Pair base-class signature ever changes, the Host wrapper silently stops overriding and the base implementation is called instead of the KOKKOS one - the compiler cannot warn without 'override'.
suggested_fix: Add 'override' to the five PairSNAPKokkosHost declarations.

summary: TagPairReaxBondOrder2 writes d_CdDelta[j] for its neighbours j, which is a redundant benign data race with the thread that owns atom j (and with the already-executed zeroing kernel).
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2205-2211 'd_Cdbo(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_Cdbopi(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_Cdbopi2(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_CdDelta[j] = 0.0; } d_CdDelta[i] = 0.0;' - d_CdDelta[j] belongs to another thread's atom.  d_CdDelta was already zeroed for all nmax entries by TagPairReaxZero (:1594 'd_CdDelta(n) = 0;') which runs earlier in compute() (:855).
failure_scenario: Both threads store 0.0 so the value is correct, but it is a concurrent unsynchronised write that thread sanitizers and Kokkos debug tooling flag, and it hides the fact that the write is dead.
suggested_fix: Delete the 'd_CdDelta[j] = 0.0;' (and the redundant 'd_CdDelta[i] = 0.0;') lines - TagPairReaxZero already covers them.

summary: v_tally3_atom() is dead code that would race if it were ever used, because it writes d_vatom directly instead of through the scatter/atomic view.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4026-4050 defines PairReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::v_tally3_atom(...) with ':4047-4049 if (vflag_atom) { for (int n = 0; n < 6; n++) d_vatom(i,n) += v[n]; }' - a plain non-atomic read-modify-write, unlike v_tally/v_tally3/v_tally4 which all go through ScatterViewHelper (:3934-3935, :3952-3953, :4013-4014).  grep over the file shows no call site (the only occurrences are the declaration pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:437 and this definition).
failure_scenario: No effect today; if anyone wires it up, per-atom virials would be silently corrupted under HALFTHREAD/GPU.
suggested_fix: Remove v_tally3_atom (declaration and definition), or convert it to the ScatterView pattern and template it on NEIGHFLAG like the other tally helpers.

summary: Inner loop counters shadow the pack-decoded atom indices j and k in ComputeAngularPreprocessed, making the kernel very easy to break.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2740-2741 'const int j = pack.i1; const int k = pack.i2;' then :2769 'for (int j = 0; j < 3; j++) fitmp[j] = 0.0;' and :2783 'for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) fjtmp[k] = 0.0;'.  The loop variables shadow the atom indices; the code is correct only because the uses at :2771-2773 and :2785-2787 are outside the loop scope.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers today, but any edit that moves a use of j or k inside one of those loops silently reads a component index instead of an atom index.
suggested_fix: Rename the loop counters (e.g. 'for (int d = 0; d < 3; d++)') as the rest of the kernel does.

summary: TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh is declared with an operator() but is never defined nor dispatched.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:52 'struct TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh{};' and :169-171 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator()(TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh, const int&) const;'.  grep for 'ShortNeigh' over src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp returns no hits, so there is neither a definition nor a parallel_for using it.
failure_scenario: None - dead declaration only; it misleads readers into thinking a short-neighbor-list path exists.
suggested_fix: Delete the tag struct and the operator() declaration.

summary: The Kokkos neighbour screening drops the base class' 'rsq > 1e-20' guard, so a coincident pair produces a division by zero (NaN energies/forces).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:553 'if (rsq < l_rcutsq) count++;' and :605 'if (rsq >= l_rcutsq) return;' versus src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:388 'if (rsq < rcutsq && rsq > 1e-20) {' (also pair_pod.cpp:416 and :451).  radialbasis then divides by dij (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:633-635 'dr1 = xij1/dij;') and angularbasis divides by dij3 (:760).
failure_scenario: Two atoms at identical coordinates (overlapping insertion, fix deposit failure, zero-temperature start from a bad structure) enter the pair list -> dij == 0 -> NaN propagates into all forces and energies instead of the pair being skipped as in the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Add the '&& rsq > 1e-20' condition to both the NeighborCount and NeighborList screening tests so the two styles select the same pairs.

summary: Fixed-size stack array 'double tm[10]' in the multi-element radialangularsum kernel overflows when the POD model has more than 10 elements.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:849-858: 'double tm[10]; for (int j=0; j<l_nelements; j++) tm[j] = 0; ... tm[tn] += ...; for (int j=0; j<l_nelements; j++) l_sumU(j + kmi) = ...' with no bound on l_nelements.  (The CPU code has the same 'double sum[10]' at src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:995, and nothing in EAPOD limits nelements.)
failure_scenario: A POD potential fitted for 11 or more elements -> out-of-bounds stack writes inside a device kernel -> silent corruption or crash.
suggested_fix: Add an explicit check in coeff()/copy_from_pod_class() that nelements <= 10, or size the scratch from nelements via team scratch memory.

summary: snap_dispatch_fused_deidrj_all() sets the policy LaunchBounds from team_size_compute_fused_deidrj but launches with team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, so the compiler is told a larger maximum block size than is ever used.
evidence: pair_snap_kokkos.h:273 'SnapAoSoATeamPolicy<DeviceType, team_size_compute_fused_deidrj, TagPairSNAPComputeFusedDeidrjAll> policy_fused_deidrj_all(n_teams_div, team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, vector_length);' - the second template argument feeds LaunchBounds (:183-184 'Kokkos::LaunchBounds<vector_length * num_teams>') while the runtime team size is team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, which is strictly smaller (e.g. 2 vs 4 for HIP, :107-108, and 2 vs 4 / 1 vs 2 for CUDA, :143-144).
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers, but the kernel is compiled for twice the block size it is launched with, so the register budget per thread (and hence occupancy/performance) is worse than intended.
suggested_fix: Use team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all as the LaunchBounds template argument for this dispatch.

summary: compute() reuses a single EV_FLOAT_REAX 'ev' across all kernel dispatches and unconditionally does 'ev_all += ev' after each section, so a section that ran parallel_for (no reduction) adds the previous section's reduction result a second time.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:775 'EV_FLOAT_REAX ev; EV_FLOAT_REAX ev_all;' then :918-932 'if (eflag_either) parallel_reduce(...ComputeBond1<HALF,1>...,*this,ev); else parallel_for(...ComputeBond1<HALF,0>...,*this); ev_all += ev;' - in the else branch ev still holds the LJ/Coulomb reduction from :809-816.  The same shape appears at :941/:948 (Multi2, guarded by eflag_either), :992/:998, :1011/:1017, :1030/:1036 (guarded by evflag) and :1056/:1065 (Bond2, guarded by vflag_either).
failure_scenario: Benign today only because the custom ev_setup (:4100-4105) forces vflag_global = 0 for the VIRIAL_FDOTR path that reaxff always takes, so ev.v[] is never filled, and evdwl/ecoul are guarded by eflag_global which implies eflag_either.  Any future change that writes ev.evdwl/ev.ecoul/ev.v in ComputeHydrogen, ComputeTorsion or ComputeLJCoulomb outside those guards silently double counts the energy or virial.
suggested_fix: Reset ev (ev = EV_FLOAT_REAX();) before each section, or move 'ev_all += ev;' inside the reduction branch.

summary: The neighbor-index blocking buffer stores the neighbor index in an unsigned short, truncating for atoms with more than 65535 neighbours in the nonbonded list.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:118 'using blocking_t = unsigned short int;'; pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1633 'blocking_t selected_jj[blocksize];' and :1653 'selected_jj[nnz] = jj_current;' where jj_current runs to jnum-1 = d_numneigh[i]-1 (:1621).  Same at :1768/:1789.
failure_scenario: A very large nonb_cut or a pathologically dense system giving an atom >65535 entries in its half neighbor list: the stored index wraps and the wrong neighbor is used for the bond-order list, producing wrong bonds and forces with no diagnostic.
suggested_fix: Use int for selected_jj, or add a check that d_numneigh[i] fits in blocking_t.
